advances: In the canonical zero-fresh hard square instance, the complete-core inequality already forces every positive physical fiber and every whole square label to have mass at most \(64\,2^{-n}G\).  Independently, each prescribed whole-label barycenter is realizable at its physical target at the label's full mass.  Consequently one may legally retain the heaviest whole label at every distinct target, with all physical target collisions aggregated before selection.  No constant fraction of the total square mass is asserted.
author: research-agent
proof:
Every positive reservoir edge is unordered and off-diagonal, so reversing the finite endpoint-edge sums in (3) gives
\[
 \sum_z\delta_z=2\sum_er_e=2Q.
\tag{17}
\]
Using \(\delta_z\leq a_z/4\) and summing over the positive fiber support yields
\[
 2Q\leq\frac14\sum_{z\in I_+}a_z=\frac W4.
\tag{18}
\]
This proves (9).

Fix \(t\in I_+\).  Apply the uniform low-rank slice theorem of accepted fact `8aac56c49321466c` to the affine slice \(A=\{t\}\).  Its intrinsic base rank is zero and its slice mass is \(W_A=a_t\), so that theorem gives
\[
 G\geq\frac1{64}\min\{W,2^na_t\}.
\tag{19}
\]
The first entry cannot attain this minimum in the hard instance: by (4) and (9),
\[
 G<\frac Q{100}<\frac Q8\leq\frac W{64}.
\tag{20}
\]
Therefore (19) uses its second entry and gives
\[
 G\geq\frac{2^na_t}{64}.
\tag{21}
\]
This is the first inequality in (10); the second follows from (4).

Fix \(\sigma\in\mathcal L^\square\).  In the canonical square notation, one of its tagged opposite pairs can be written
\[
 u=t(\sigma)+h,
 \qquad
 v=t(\sigma)-h.
\tag{22}
\]
Suppose first that \(u\ne v\).  Each of these two tagged occurrences contributes \(\theta_\sigma\) to its physical load in (6), regardless of any additional collision with other labels or with the other opposite pair.  Hence
\[
 a_u\geq R_u\geq\theta_\sigma,
 \qquad
 a_v\geq R_v\geq\theta_\sigma.
\tag{23}
\]
Let \(A=\operatorname{aff}\{u,v\}\).  The positive-fiber points on this affine line span a space of intrinsic rank one, and its total fiber mass obeys
\[
 W_A:=\sum_{z\in I_+\cap A}a_z
 \geq a_u+a_v
 \geq2\theta_\sigma.
\tag{24}
\]
Accepted fact `8aac56c49321466c` now gives
\[
 G\geq\frac1{64}\min\{W,2^{n-1}W_A\}.
\tag{25}
\]
Equation (20) again excludes the \(W\)-entry.  Using (24) in the remaining entry gives
\[
 G\geq\frac{2^{n-1}W_A}{64}
 \geq\frac{2^n\theta_\sigma}{64},
\tag{26}
\]
which proves the first inequality in (11).

Suppose instead that \(u=v\).  Then \(h=0\), and the same physical source appears twice as two tagged occurrences of this label.  Exact multiplicity in (6) gives
\[
 a_u\geq R_u\geq2\theta_\sigma.
\tag{27}
\]
Apply the rank-zero estimate (21) at \(u\), then use (27):
\[
 G\geq\frac{2^na_u}{64}
 \geq\frac{2^{n+1}\theta_\sigma}{64}.
\tag{28}
\]
This proves (12), and hence (11), in the loop case.  Equations (23) and (27) use aggregate physical loads, so cross-label source reuse and cross-pair physical collisions cannot invalidate them.  The strict comparison with \(Q\) in (11) follows from (4).

We prove the individual target realization.  Fix \(\sigma\in\mathcal L^\square\).  For every tagged occurrence \(y=y_{\sigma,o}\), exact multiplicity in (6) gives
\[
 0<\theta_\sigma\leq a_y.
\tag{29}
\]
The constant density
\[
 f_{\sigma,o}(x):=
 \frac{\theta_\sigma}{a_y}\mathbf1_{C_y}(x)
\tag{30}
\]
has mass \(\theta_\sigma\) and barycenter \(c_y\).  Thus
\[
 c_y\in\mathsf M_{\theta_\sigma}(C_y).
\tag{31}
\]
Put \(s:=\theta_\sigma^{1/d}>0\).  The positive-root fiber-metronoid convexity proved in accepted fact `dfd25e72c1f45a4e`, applied successively to the four equal-root triples
\[
 (y_{\sigma,o},c_{y_{\sigma,o}},s),
 \qquad o=1,2,3,4,
\tag{32}
\]
shows that their equal average is again a legal positive-root triple.  Equations (5) and (8) identify that average as
\[
 \left(t(\sigma),r_\sigma^c,s\right).
\tag{33}
\]
Since its root remains \(s\), its packet mass is \(s^d=\theta_\sigma\).  Hence
\[
 r_\sigma^c\in\mathsf M_{\theta_\sigma}(C_{t(\sigma)}),
\tag{34}
\]
which proves (14).  If tags repeat, the same positive-root triple is repeated with its tagged multiplicity in (32); this is an individual membership proof and does not add independently constructed densities for two different labels.

It remains to prove (16).  The family \(\Gamma\) is finite.  For each distinct physical target \(t\in t(\Gamma)\), choose one label
\[
 \sigma_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\substack{\sigma\in\Gamma\\t(\sigma)=t}}
 \theta_\sigma.
\tag{35}
\]
By (14), choose one density \(h_{\sigma_t}\leq1\) on \(C_t\) of mass \(\theta_{\sigma_t}\) and barycenter \(r_{\sigma_t}^c\).  Put
\[
 q_{\sigma_t}:=\theta_{\sigma_t},
 \qquad
 q_\sigma:=0\quad(\sigma\ne\sigma_t),
\tag{36}
\]
and assign the zero density to every unselected label.  Exactly one nonzero density is used at each distinct physical target, so every collision class in (15) has pointwise sum at most one.  Thus (36) is one jointly feasible target family of total mass
\[
 \sum_{t\in t(\Gamma)}\theta_{\sigma_t}
 =
 \sum_{t\in t(\Gamma)}
 \max_{\substack{\sigma\in\Gamma\\t(\sigma)=t}}
 \theta_\sigma.
\tag{37}
\]
Taking the supremum in (15) proves (16).  No target density belonging to a second label at the same physical target has been added, and no local core or individual target realization has been summed as a complete-core capacity.
statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body of positive mixed volume, and write
\[
 C_z:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(z,x)\in C\},
 \qquad
 a_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z),
 \qquad
 I_+:=\{z\in\mathbb Z^n:a_z>0\},
\tag{1}
\]
\[
 W:=\sum_{z\in I_+}a_z,
 \qquad
 G:=\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{core}}(C).
\tag{2}
\]
Retain one common canonical zero-fresh hard instance of accepted facts `6bfe50fed9a5540b` and `6e6a3b541bc64f05`.  Thus the half-strength reservoir \(r=(r_e)\) has positive unordered off-diagonal edges, mass and endpoint degrees
\[
 Q:=\sum_er_e>0,
 \qquad
 \delta_z:=d_z(r)=\sum_{e\ni z}r_e
 \leq\frac{a_z}{4},
\tag{3}
\]
and the hard ledger gives
\[
 G<\frac Q{100}.
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(\mathcal L^\square\) be the canonical degree-weighted complete-product whole-label family from `6e6a3b541bc64f05`.  Every
\(\sigma\in\mathcal L^\square\) has mass \(\theta_\sigma>0\), physical target \(t(\sigma)\in\mathbb Z^n\), and a four-entry tagged occurrence multiset
\[
 \mathcal O_\sigma=
 [y_{\sigma,1},y_{\sigma,2},y_{\sigma,3},y_{\sigma,4}],
 \qquad
 \frac14\sum_{o=1}^4y_{\sigma,o}=t(\sigma),
\tag{5}
\]
where loops and repeated physical sources remain separate tags.  Its physical occurrence loads satisfy
\[
 R_z:=\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal L^\square}
 \theta_\sigma\operatorname{mult}_z(\mathcal O_\sigma)
 \leq a_z.
\tag{6}
\]
For every occurrence source put
\[
 c_z:=\frac1{a_z}\int_{C_z}x\,dx,
\tag{7}
\]
and define, for every whole label,
\[
 r_\sigma^c:=\frac14\sum_{o=1}^4c_{y_{\sigma,o}}.
\tag{8}
\]

Then
\[
 \boxed{W\geq8Q.}
\tag{9}
\]
Every positive physical fiber satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 a_t\leq64\,2^{-n}G
 <\frac{16}{25}\,2^{-n}Q
 \qquad(t\in I_+).}
\tag{10}
\]
Every whole-label mass satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \theta_\sigma\leq64\,2^{-n}G
 <\frac{16}{25}\,2^{-n}Q
 \qquad(\sigma\in\mathcal L^\square).}
\tag{11}
\]
If one tagged opposite pair of \(\sigma\) is a loop, the stronger bound
\[
 \theta_\sigma\leq32\,2^{-n}G
\tag{12}
\]
holds.  All bounds retain repeated-tag multiplicity and arbitrary reuse of one physical source by different labels.

For
\[
 \mathsf M_m(C_t):=
 \left\{
 \frac1m\int_{C_t}x f(x)\,dx:
 0\leq f\leq1\ \text{a.e.},\quad
 \int_{C_t}f=m
 \right\},
\tag{13}
\]
every prescribed whole-label barycenter is individually realizable at full label mass in its physical target:
\[
 \boxed{
 r_\sigma^c\in
 \mathsf M_{\theta_\sigma}(C_{t(\sigma)})
 \qquad(\sigma\in\mathcal L^\square).}
\tag{14}
\]

Finally retain the positive whole-label subfamily \(\Gamma\subseteq\mathcal L^\square\) of accepted fact `6e6a3b541bc64f05`, and define its exact prescribed-barycenter target-packing capacity by
\[
 \mathsf P_\Gamma:=
 \sup\left\{
 \sum_{\sigma\in\Gamma}q_\sigma:
 \begin{array}{l}
 0\leq q_\sigma\leq\theta_\sigma,\\
 h_\sigma:C_{t(\sigma)}\to[0,\infty)\text{ measurable},\\
 \displaystyle\int_{C_{t(\sigma)}}h_\sigma=q_\sigma,\quad
 \displaystyle\int_{C_{t(\sigma)}}x h_\sigma(x)\,dx
 =q_\sigma r_\sigma^c,\\
 \displaystyle
 \sum_{\sigma\in\Gamma:t(\sigma)=t}h_\sigma\leq1
 \text{ a.e. on }C_t\text{ for every physical target }t
 \end{array}
 \right\}.
\tag{15}
\]
Then the collision-safe legal lower bound is
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathsf P_\Gamma
 \geq
 \sum_{t\in t(\Gamma)}
 \max_{\substack{\sigma\in\Gamma\\t(\sigma)=t}}
 \theta_\sigma.}
\tag{16}
\]
No lower bound on the right side of (16) as an absolute fraction of
\(\sum_{\sigma\in\Gamma}\theta_\sigma\) is asserted.
